content: ELMO1, also known as Engulfment and Cell Motility Protein 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the ELMO1 gene. In humans, the ELMO1 gene is located on chromosome 7, while in mice, it is found on chromosome 13. Structure The human ELMO1 protein consists of 720 amino acid residues. It contains three distinct domains: 1. An N-terminal Armadillo domain, spanning residues 82 to 262. 2. A central ELMO (Engulfment and Cell Motility) domain, spanning residues 301 to 492. 3. A C-terminal pleckstrin homology (PH) domain, spanning residues 527 to 674. Additionally, ELMO1 has a proline-rich motif at its extreme C-terminus. Secondary structure analysis predicts the presence of alpha-helical regions at both the Nand C-termini. The structure of the pleckstrin homology domain of ELMO1 has been determined using X-ray crystallography. Function The protein encoded by the ELMO1 gene interacts with the Dedicator of Cytokinesis 1 (DOCK180) protein to facilitate phagocytosis and mediate changes in cell shape. Its similarity to a protein in Caenorhabditis elegans suggests that ELMO1 may also play roles in apoptosis and cell migration. Alternative splicing of the ELMO1 gene results in multiple transcript variants encoding different isoforms. Interactions ELMO1 has been shown to interact with DOCK180 and HCK. Specifically: ELMO1 directly binds to the SH3 domain of HCK, and this interaction depends on polyproline motifs. When ELMO1 forms a complex with DOCK180, it activates Rac GTPase-dependent biological processes. The PH domain of ELMO1 stabilizes DOCK180, protecting it from degradation. Binding of ELMO1 to DOCK180 alleviates steric inhibition of DOCK180, enabling it to activate Rac GTPase. The proline-rich motif at the C-terminus of ELMO1 is critical for its binding to the SH3 domain at the N-terminus of DOCK180. The ELMO1-DOCK180 complex acts as a regulator of Rac during cell development and migration. Mutations in the interaction sites for DOCK180 on ELMO1 disrupt the formation of the ELMO1-DOCK180 complex. When ELMO1 forms a complex with both DOCK180 and CrkII, it achieves maximal efficiency in promoting phagocytosis. This molecular complex functions upstream of Rac during the phagocytic process.
